welcome: Every essence is an extension of its master's will. But a reaper's path begins long before the blade is forged — power must first be found and brought under control. Only then will it take a form that can serve in battle and in labor. Only in the hands of a reaper devoted to the craft will that power reveal its true potential.
Every element is gathered here. The image beside each name leads to the same path as its bookmark.
bloody_scythe: Blood answers violence with violence. Its essence does not come from ore or crop, but from lives whose deaths leave enough force behind to stain the world itself. A Bloody Scythe rewards a wielder who remains close, wounded and relentless.

Bloody Essence cannot be shaped at a crafting table. Villagers have a ${balance:Drops.VILLAGER_DROP_CHANCE|percent}% chance to leave one behind when slain by a player. Another player may leave one with a ${balance:Drops.PLAYER_DROP_CHANCE|percent}% chance, provided the killer and victim are not allied.

The essence is already complete when it appears: a clot of concentrated life-force that needs no second binding. Keep it intact. Its purpose is not to be diluted, but to be set into a weapon capable of surviving what follows.

Two Netherite Ingots form the cutting edge, two sticks the long haft, and Bloody Essence seals the empty side of the pattern. The result keeps the common scythe frame: ${balance:Base.DURABILITY} durability and a swift, heavy sweep.

Each strike has a ${balance:Blood.BLEEDING_CHANCE|percent}% chance to open Bleeding. Vampirism has a ${balance:Vampirism.VAMPIRISM_CHANCE|percent}% chance to return ${balance:Vampirism.HEAL_FRACTION|percent}% of dealt damage as health. A separate ${balance:Blood.DEFENSE_PIERCE_CHANCE|percent}% chance lets the blow ignore ${balance:Blood.DEFENSE_PIERCE_MITIGATION_IGNORED|percent}% of the target's protection.

Right click to seize enemies within ${balance:Blood.BLENDER_RADIUS|number} blocks. The scythe strikes twice, drags victims inward and leaves Slowness II and Bleeding II behind. The rite costs ${balance:Blood.BLENDER_DURABILITY_COST} durability and rests for ${balance:Blood.BLENDER_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

Invoke the ability key and the hunt begins. For ${balance:BloodHarvest.KILL_WINDOW_TICKS|seconds} seconds, prey within ${balance:BloodHarvest.RADIUS|number} blocks is marked for the harvest. Success grants a brief surge of speed, strength and regeneration; failure answers with weakness and hindrance. The rite costs ${balance:BloodHarvest.DURABILITY_COST} durability and has a ${balance:BloodHarvest.COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds}-second cooldown.

Do not treat this element as a duelist's weapon. It grows dangerous when several enemies are close enough for Blender and when the wielder accepts damage in exchange for pressure. Bleeding softens the field, vampirism buys time, and Blood Harvest turns a crowded fight into a wager.
toxic_scythe: Venom is patient. It seeps through armor, denies recovery and turns a crowded battlefield into hostile ground. Toxic power is not gathered from one monster; it is distilled by forcing several kinds of poison into a single stable essence.

Prepare five Spider Eyes, one Pufferfish and four potions of Poison II. Ordinary poison is too weak for the binding: each potion must be the strengthened form. The ingredients are arranged around the pufferfish so that no side of the mixture remains unpoisoned.
When the nine reagents meet, the separate poisons stop competing and collapse into one green core. The essence remembers both the bite of venom and the corrosive attack on equipment.
Set Toxic Essence into the common Netherite scythe frame. The weapon keeps the familiar weight and reach, but the edge becomes a carrier for toxins rather than a simple cutting surface.

Each hit has a ${balance:Toxic.PASSIVE_ARMOR_DAMAGE_CHANCE|percent}% chance to damage worn armor and a ${balance:Toxic.PASSIVE_POISON_CHANCE|percent}% chance to inflict Poison II. The effects are independent, so a single strike may wound flesh, equipment or both.

Right click to launch a dense globe of poison. On impact it spreads through a ${balance:ToxicOrb.DAMAGE_RADIUS|number}-block radius, deals ${balance:ToxicOrb.PURE_DAMAGE|number} pure damage, inflicts Poison II and tears ${balance:ToxicOrb.ARMOR_DAMAGE} durability from armor. Cost: ${balance:Toxic.ORB_DURABILITY_COST} durability. Cooldown: ${balance:Toxic.ORB_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

The ability key releases the essence around the wielder for ${balance:ToxicAura.DURATION_TICKS|seconds} seconds. Enemies within ${balance:ToxicAura.RADIUS|number} blocks are poisoned, their armor is continuously worn down, and the miasma may deal pure damage or nausea. Cost: ${balance:ToxicAura.AURA_DURABILITY_COST} durability. Cooldown: ${balance:ToxicAura.AURA_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

Toxic favors long pressure over one clean blow. Keep armored enemies inside the aura, use the orb to begin a fight before they close the distance, and let corrosion make every later strike more valuable than the first.
withering_scythe: The Wither does not merely kill; it leaves a hunger that continues after the victim falls. Withering Essence binds that hunger to a weapon and gives the wielder a second resource besides durability: souls.

The rite calls for four Bones, two Netherite Ingots, two Wither Skeleton Skulls and a Nether Star. None is ornamental. Bone gives form, skulls give memory, Netherite gives endurance, and the star gives the whole pattern a heart that refuses to die.

Place the Nether Star at the center, skulls to either side, Netherite above and below, and bones in the corners. The finished essence feels less like an object than a sealed command waiting for servants.
Bind the essence to the common Netherite scythe frame. From this moment, kills are no longer only victories; they become fuel for whatever the blade will call next.

Hits have a ${balance:Withering.WITHER_CHANCE|percent}% chance to inflict Wither II. A slain mob yields ${balance:Withering.SOULS_PER_MOB_KILL} soul, while a slain player yields ${balance:Withering.SOULS_PER_PLAYER_KILL}. Souls remain stored for summoning rather than vanishing with the corpse.

Right click to spend ${balance:Withering.MINION_SOUL_COST} souls and ${balance:Withering.MINION_DURABILITY_COST} durability, calling a fire-immune Withering minion to your side. Its kills feed souls back into your Withering Scythe. Dismissing it, or letting its lifetime expire, refunds up to ${balance:Withering.MINION_SOUL_COST} souls in proportion to its remaining health, rounded down. Without further enchantment the bond can sustain up to ${balance:Withering.MAX_MINIONS} servants at once.

The ability key opens the seal for ${balance:WitheringAura.DURATION_TICKS|seconds} seconds. Enemies within ${balance:WitheringAura.WITHER_RADIUS|number} blocks suffer Wither II. Allied minions within ${balance:WitheringAura.MINION_BUFF_RADIUS|number} blocks continuously receive a ${balance:WitheringAura.MINION_BUFF_TICKS|seconds}-second Strength and Speed buff, refreshed while they remain inside the aura. Cost: ${balance:WitheringAura.AURA_DURABILITY_COST} durability. Cooldown: ${balance:WitheringAura.AURA_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

This path is strongest when prepared before danger arrives. Bank souls, enter battle with room for minions, then release the aura only when both enemies and servants can be caught in it. The element rewards command more than haste.
golden_scythe: Gold is soft in the hand and merciless in desire. Bound around a Nether Star, it becomes an essence of fortune, ownership and execution. The Golden path does not merely defeat enemies; it insists that their defeat be profitable.
Prepare four Gold Nuggets, four Blocks of Gold and one Nether Star. The cost is deliberate. Golden power only answers when wealth surrounds power from every side.

Seal the Nether Star at the center of a ring of gold. Blocks carry the weight of the offering; nuggets close the corners. When the pattern is complete, the metal no longer feels inert—it feels expectant.
Set Golden Essence into the common Netherite scythe frame. The finished edge is still a weapon, but every cut now carries the promise that something valuable should remain when the fight ends.
While held, the scythe grants +${balance:Golden.PASSIVE_LOOTING_BONUS} Looting to its kills. Piglins also read the golden bond as familiar wealth and remain neutral as though the wielder wore gold.

Right click a target within ${balance:Golden.MIDAS_REACH|number} blocks to strike for ${balance:Golden.MIDAS_DAMAGE_FRACTION|percent}% of maximum health as true damage, clamped between ${balance:Golden.MIDAS_MIN_DAMAGE|number} and ${balance:Golden.MIDAS_MAX_DAMAGE|number}. The victim is marked for +${balance:Golden.MARK_LOOTING_BONUS} Looting. Cost: ${balance:Golden.MIDAS_DURABILITY_COST} durability. Cooldown: ${balance:Golden.MIDAS_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

The ability key casts the mark across enemies in a ${balance:GoldenRain.RADIUS|number}-block radius. Marked foes carry the same +${balance:Golden.MARK_LOOTING_BONUS} Looting promise into death. The rite costs ${balance:GoldenRain.DURABILITY_COST} durability and requires ${balance:GoldenRain.COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds before it can be called again.

Save Midas Touch for prey whose health pool justifies the execution. Golden Rain belongs to crowded hunts and farms where many valuable drops are about to fall at once. The element wastes power on enemies with nothing worth claiming.
frozen_scythe: Cold preserves what fire consumes. The Frozen path begins with a heart that has forgotten warmth, then cages that stillness inside blue ice until the essence can be carried by steel.

A Frozen Heart has a ${balance:Drops.HEART_CHANCE|percent}% chance to appear in the spoils of Strays and in igloo chests. There is a darker path as well: a player who dies to freezing while caught in powder snow leaves one behind.
Place the Frozen Heart at the center, Blue Ice along the four sides and Powder Snow Buckets in the corners. The heart gives the cold a will; the ice gives it permanence; the snow gives it motion.
Bind Frozen Essence into the common Netherite scythe frame. The metal remains dark, but the edge carries a cold that clings to terrain and flesh long after the swing has passed.

The wielder moves through powder snow without its usual punishment and carries Frost Walker ${balance:Frozen.COLD_MASTER_FROST_WALKER_LEVEL|roman}. Each hit also has a ${balance:Frozen.COLD_MASTER_FREEZING_CHANCE|percent}% chance to inflict Freezing.

Right click to cast a fast shard of ice. A direct hit deals ${balance:IceSpike.HIT_DAMAGE|number} damage and applies Freezing. The shot costs ${balance:Frozen.ICE_SPIKE_DURABILITY_COST} durability and rests for ${balance:Frozen.ICE_SPIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

The ability key breaks the stored winter loose across a ${balance:FrozenStorm.RADIUS|number}-block radius. Enemies are struck with Freezing, Slowness and Weakness. Cost: ${balance:FrozenStorm.DURABILITY_COST} durability. Cooldown: ${balance:FrozenStorm.COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.
Frozen is a weapon of position. Slow the field, deny pursuit and turn dangerous ground into safe ground before committing to the kill. The spike punishes distance; the storm punishes numbers.
farmer_scythe: Not every essence is born from death. The Farmer path binds the stubborn rhythm of crops, soil and seasons into a tool that can reap an entire field without forgetting that the next harvest must still be planted.

Prepare four Ender Pearls, then Beetroot, Carrot, Chorus Fruit, Potato and Wheat. The pearls bind distant patches of earth into one reach, while the crops teach the essence what must be harvested and what must be returned to the soil.
The Chorus Fruit rests at the center. Carrot and Potato stand at its sides, Beetroot above and Wheat below, all held in place by Ender Pearls at the corners.

The familiar scythe pattern still uses Netherite and sticks, but Farmer Essence changes the weapon's nature. Its base damage follows a Netherite Hoe rather than the martial scythes, while its durability remains ${balance:Base.DURABILITY}.

Mature crops have a ${balance:Farmer.DOUBLE_DROP_CHANCE|percent}% chance to double their final drops after Fortune. Right click a mature crop to reap and immediately replant it. Right click tillable ground to prepare a ${balance:Farmer.TILLING_DIAMETER}x${balance:Farmer.TILLING_DIAMETER} patch, and every resulting farmland block is fully hydrated at once.

Sneak and right click to reap mature crops throughout a ${balance:Farmer.MASS_HARVEST_RADIUS|number}-block radius. The passive double-yield chance is applied to every harvest, crops are replanted and the gathered produce is placed directly into the wielder's inventory. Cost: ${balance:Farmer.MASS_HARVEST_DURABILITY_COST} durability. Cooldown: ${balance:Farmer.MASS_HARVEST_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

The ability key pushes nearby crops forward by ${balance:Farmer.GROWTH_REDUCTION_FRACTION|percent}% of their remaining growth within ${balance:Farmer.GROWTH_ACCELERATION_RADIUS|number} blocks. Each planting may receive this blessing once. The rite consumes ${balance:Farmer.GROWTH_BONE_MEAL_COST} bone meal and ${balance:Farmer.GROWTH_DURABILITY_COST} durability, then rests for ${balance:Farmer.GROWTH_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

Treat the scythe as the heart of a field rather than a weapon. Prepare soil in broad passes, reap by hand when precision matters, save Mass Harvest for full fields and spend Growth Acceleration only when the saved time is worth both bone meal and steel.
fire_scythe: Flame is the loudest essence: quick to awaken, eager to spread and difficult to persuade into a stable shape. Fire Essence is built from heat, pressure and controlled flight so that the blaze enters the blade without consuming it.

Prepare two Blaze Powder, one Fire Charge, two Lava Buckets, one TNT block and three plain Firework Rockets. The rockets must be Flight 1 and carry no explosion; the binding needs thrust, not a second detonation.

Blaze Powder and Fire Charge crown the pattern, lava flanks the TNT core, and the three empty rockets close the lower edge. The lava is consumed, but the iron buckets remain behind like the pans of a completed rite.
Set Fire Essence into the common Netherite scythe frame. Fire follows the sword-born combat lineage and carries the same martial base as the other combat elements.

Every strike ignites its victim. Each hit also has a ${balance:Fire.PASSIVE_BURNS_CHANCE|percent}% chance to apply Burns for ${balance:Fire.PASSIVE_BURNS_TICKS|seconds} seconds; the passive only refreshes when at most one second remains. While held in either hand, the scythe lets its wielder walk on lava and ignore magma-block damage.

Hold RMB for ${balance:Fire.FIREBALL_CHARGE_TICKS|seconds} second to lock a highlighted enemy, then release. The fireball homes on that target for up to ${balance:Fire.FIREBALL_MAX_LIFETIME_TICKS|seconds} seconds before exploding. Its blast reaches about ${balance:Fire.FIREBALL_EXPLOSION_RADIUS|number} blocks, deals up to ${balance:Fire.FIREBALL_MAX_DAMAGE|number} explosion damage with distance falloff and never breaks blocks. The locked target is ignited, receives Burns for ${balance:Fire.FIREBALL_BURNS_TICKS|seconds} seconds and is stunned for ${balance:Fire.FIREBALL_STUN_TICKS|seconds} seconds. Cost: ${balance:Fire.FIREBALL_DURABILITY_COST} durability. Cooldown: ${balance:Fire.FIREBALL_COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds.

The ability key ignites every valid enemy within ${balance:FireBurst.RADIUS|number} blocks, applies Burns for ${balance:FireBurst.BURNS_TICKS|seconds} seconds and damages each non-Netherite armor piece by ${balance:FireBurst.ARMOR_DAMAGE} durability. After ${balance:FireBurst.LAUNCH_DELAY_TICKS|seconds} second the marked targets erupt upward through a cloud of flame. Cost: ${balance:FireBurst.DURABILITY_COST} durability. Cooldown: ${balance:FireBurst.COOLDOWN_TICKS|seconds} seconds. Pets and teammates are ignored.

Burns blocks healing completely while active. A target can suffer it continuously for at most ${balance:Burns.MAX_CONTINUOUS_TICKS|seconds} seconds; when Burns ends, or reaches that cap, the target gains a hidden ${balance:Burns.IMMUNITY_TICKS|seconds}-second immunity to new Burns applications.
Fire wins by denying recovery and forcing movement. Inferno breaks grouped enemies apart, while Hunting Fireball keeps pressure on a chosen target that tries to disengage.
